title: Read: hiragana, step by step
description: Learn to read Japanese sounds, a few characters at a time.

units.title: The five vowels
intro: Japanese is written with three scripts mixed together. Hiragana is the one to learn first. It has 46 characters.
Each hiragana character is one sound. Unlike English letters, a character is always read the same way.
Japanese has only five vowel sounds: a, i, u, e, o. Always in that order. Every other character is a consonant plus one of these five.
How they sound: a = 'ah' as in father. i = 'ee' as in see. u = 'oo' as in food. e = 'eh' as in bed. o = 'oh' as in go. Keep each one short.
The text under each character (like 'a') is romaji: Japanese sounds spelled with English letters. It is only a helper.

items.hint: Sounds like 'ah'. Look for a capital A hiding in the middle: crossing strokes over a loop.
Sounds like 'ee'. Two strokes side by side, like two eels swimming together.
Sounds like 'oo'. A dash above a bent line, like someone hit in the belly going 'oof'.
Sounds like 'eh'. A runner full of energy: a dash for the head, legs stretched out.
Sounds like 'oh'. Close to あ, but with an extra dot on the right: 'oh, a dot!'

units.title: The K row
intro: Now put a k sound in front of each vowel: ka, ki, ku, ke, ko.
Same vowel order as before: a, i, u, e, o. Every row in the hiragana chart follows it.
After this unit you can read real words made of vowels and K sounds.

items.hint: A blade swinging down with a spark flying off: 'ka!' like a karate chop.
Looks like an old key with two teeth on top.
An open bird beak calling 'coo, coo'.
A post on the left and a gate on the right. 'ke' as in 'kept': the gate is kept shut.
Two short curved lines, like two koi fish swimming.

units.title: The S row
intro: The S row: sa, shi, su, se, so.
One surprise: the second one is 'shi', not 'si'. Japanese has no 'si' sound.
さ looks a lot like き from the last unit. さ has one bar, き has two.

items.hint: Like き with only one bar. Picture a salmon jumping up a stream.
A fishing hook. She is fishing: 'shi'.
A line with a loop, like a curly straw. Sip some soup: 'su'.
Looks like a seat with a back. 'se' as in 'set'.
One zigzag stroke, like thread when you sew: 'so'.

units.title: The T row
intro: The T row: ta, chi, tsu, te, to.
Two surprises this time. The second is 'chi', not 'ti'. The third is 'tsu', not 'tu'.
'tsu' is the sound at the end of 'cats', then 'oo'. It is one beat, not two.

items.hint: Looks like a small t and a small a squeezed together: 'ta'.
Like the number 5 with a bar on top. 'chi' as in 'cheese'.
One sweeping curve, like a big wave: tsunami.
A bar on top with a curved tail, like a capital T bending over. 'te' as in 'ten'.
A short stick poking into a curve, like a thorn stuck in a toe: 'to'.

units.title: The N row
intro: The N row: na, ni, nu, ne, no. No surprises here.
Careful with ぬ and ね. They look alike. ぬ has two loops tangled together. ね has a straight post on the left.

items.hint: A cross, a dash, and a loop at the bottom like a knot in a rope. 'na' as in 'nacho'.
A post on the left and two short lines on the right. 'ni' sounds like 'knee'.
Tangled loops, like noodles. 'nu' as in 'noodle'.
A post on the left and a curled tail on the right, like a cat's tail. 'neko' means cat.
One swirl drawn without lifting the pen: 'no'.

units.title: The H row
intro: The H row: ha, hi, fu, he, ho.
The third one is 'fu', not 'hu'. It is a soft f: blow air between your lips without biting your lower lip.
Later you will see は read as 'wa' when it works as a grammar marker. For now it is 'ha'.

items.hint: A post on the left, then a cross with a loop at the bottom. 'ha' as in 'ha ha'.
A wide smile: 'hee hee'.
A curvy middle with small strokes around it, like a mountain with clouds: Mount Fuji.
One bent line, like a small hill. 'he' as in 'hen'.
Like は with one more bar on top, as if it put on a hat: 'ho ho'.

units.title: The M row
intro: The M row: ma, mi, mu, me, mo. No surprises in the sounds.
め looks like ぬ from the N row. め ends in a plain curve. ぬ ends in an extra loop.

items.hint: Two bars across a pole, with a loop at the foot. 'ma' as in 'mama'.
A loop with a long tail and a stroke crossing it, like a music note falling over: do, re, 'mi'.
A loop on the left, a hook and a dot on the right. A cow says 'moo': 'mu'.
Like ぬ without the last loop. 'me' is also the Japanese word for eye.
A fishing hook with two bars across it: catch 'mo'-re fish.

units.title: The Y row
intro: The Y row has only three characters: ya, yu, yo. There is no 'yi' or 'ye' in modern Japanese.
'yu' sounds like the English word 'you'.

items.hint: A curve with two strokes through it, like the horned head of a yak: 'ya'.
A loop with a line through the middle, like a fish. 'yu' sounds like 'you'.
A post with a small arm and a loop at the bottom, like a yo-yo on its string.

units.title: The R row
intro: The R row: ra, ri, ru, re, ro.
The Japanese r is not the English r. Tap the tip of your tongue once just behind your top teeth. It lands between an English r, l and d.
Three look-alikes: る ends in a loop, ろ does not. れ looks like ね, but its tail kicks outward instead of curling.

items.hint: A dash floating above a curve, like a rabbit's ear above its back: 'ra'.
Two strokes, the right one longer, like reeds by a river. 'ri' sounds like 'ree'.
A zigzag that ends in a loop: the route loops at the end, 'ru'.
A post on the left and a tail that kicks out to the right. 're' as in 'red'.
Like る with no loop: the road just ends, 'ro'.

units.title: The last three
intro: Three characters left: wa, wo and n. After this you can read all 46 basic hiragana.
を is written 'wo' in romaji but said 'o', the same as お. It is only used as a grammar marker, never inside a word.
ん is the only character with no vowel. It is a plain 'n' sound and never starts a word.

items.hint: A post on the left and one big round curve on the right, like a round belly: 'wa'.
Said 'o'. Marks the thing an action is done to. You will meet it in sentences later.
Looks like a handwritten lowercase n: 'n'.
